verdict.rationale: Baseten documents its own performance mechanisms. These include token streaming over SSE, TensorRT-optimized containers built by Truss, "high-performance LLMs" via Model APIs, and session-based routing that keeps shared prompt prefixes in the KV cache. A community report that the client, not the server, became the throughput bottleneck lends indirect support. However, no time-to-first-token or throughput figures are documented. missing for 10: quantified TTFT/latency benchmarks, documented throughput figures or tuning guidance, independent hands-on latency measurements.

support.subject: As a developer, I can serve latency-sensitive workloads with fast time-to-first-token and high-throughput generation

citations.quote: Streaming sends tokens as they are generated over server-sent events, which suits long generations and UIs where partial output beats a blank wait.
`uvx truss push` builds a TensorRT-optimized container and deploys it.
OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints for high-performance LLMs
Baseten routes requests with the same session ID to the same replica, where the shared prompt prefix is more likely to remain in the KV cache.
The Performance Client sends concurrent requests from Python, JavaScript, or Rust.
